summary: SSE session-token drift causes split final choice and duplicated metadata on reconnect
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their web app experiences a short network blip and reconnects to our SSE endpoint, the final choice from the model is split into two messages and the choice metadata (finish_reason, index) is duplicated across fragments. This results in the UI showing two partial completions and sometimes applying the finalization twice.

Impact: Affects BrazenChat's production chat sessions for ~2-3% of long-response conversations (responses > 1k tokens). Causes visible duplicate final text and duplicate message actions in the customer UI. Customer is on Dedicated plan and reports revenue-impacting user confusion.

Environment: prod serving via dedicated cluster in us-east-1. Customer front-end uses an HTTP/2 reverse proxy (Envoy) terminating to our CDN, then our streaming-proxy layer forwards to the serving runtime. Observed with both SSE (primary) and WebSocket fallback enabled.

Observed behavior: After reconnect the stream emits a fragment containing the tail of the last chunk (tokens n..m) followed by a second fragment containing an overlapping set of tokens with an end event. Both fragments include finish_reason and choice indexes; the UI treats both as separate final choices. The duplicate metadata appears correlated with reconnects where the reconnect request used a session token that differs by a single-byte from the one originally issued (token drift).

Expected behavior: On reconnect, server should stitch and deliver only the missing suffix, or send a single end/final event. Metadata (finish_reason, index) should appear once on the final stitched choice.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start long generation (>1k tokens) from BrazenChat UI against redwood/llama2-13b-instruct-q4 in us-east-1.
2) Simulate a 2-5 second client network blip (client disconnects and reconnects).
3) Client re-establishes SSE stream including resume_token header with token generated by client-side library (sometimes mutated by client-side proxy).
4) Observe server stream delivery: look for split tail fragments and duplicated finish metadata in the SSE stream.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: resume_token drift (one-byte mutation) causes streaming-proxy to treat reconnect as 'partial overlap' then cause serving-runtime to flush remaining KV cache and re-emit a small tail resulting in duplicate final event metadata.

Captured packet traces across Envoy and our CDN show single-byte differences introduced by a buggy client-side middleware that base64-escapes tokens differently under HTTP/2 header compression. Customer reproduced by toggling client middleware off; when token exact match occurs, issue not observed.

Reproduced internally: created a harness that mutates resume_token by toggling low bit; observed same split final choice and duplicated finish_reason metadata. Logs show streaming-proxy performing an overlap reconciliation path and then calling runtime.flush_tail() followed by runtime.emit_end(). The runtime does not de-duplicate emit_end() if overlap path completed earlier.
workarounds: Customer workaround: disable the client middleware that mutates resume_token (applies to BrazenChat's JS SDK).

Server-side workaround (short term): streaming-proxy can compare resume_token checksum and, on 1-byte mismatch, normalize tokens by computing canonical form before reconciliation (requires partial fix deployed to proxy).

2) Implement server-side finalization de-duplication in serving-runtime (PR opened).
3) Coordinate with SDK team to add stronger canonicalization for resume_token before network send (prevent client-side drift).
4) Postmortem and runbook update to include token-checksum mismatch handling and recommended SDK config.
